info.title: USTAZ API
info.description:
USTAZ - أستاذ. Backend API for the Egyptian teacher discovery and learning platform.

All endpoints are versioned under /api/v1. Successful responses use { success, message, data }; failures use RFC 7807 ProblemDetails with a validation `errors` dictionary where applicable.

Deliberately on the global budget rather than the credential budget: a single-page app
re-reads this on every route change and on every tab focus, which the ten-per-minute
brute-force limit would throttle into a broken session. There is nothing to brute force
here — the caller already holds a valid access token.

ApiResponse.description:
The envelope every successful USTAZ endpoint returns, so the React client can rely on
one consistent shape.

CancelGroupEnrollmentRequest.description: Optional body for the cancellation endpoints.

RefundPaymentRequest.description: Optional body for the refund endpoint.

RevokeCertificateRequest.description: Optional body for the revoke endpoint.

UpdateSubmissionRequest.description: Body for replacing a homework submission.

Bearer.description: Paste the JWT access token here. The 'Bearer ' prefix is added automatically.

tags.name: Account
tags.description:
The signed-in user's own account, regardless of which role they hold.
            
These routes exist because a profile picture is not a teacher feature. Students, parents and
administrators all have their avatar rendered across the product, but only teachers had an
endpoint to set one — so for everyone else the field stayed empty forever. Rather than add a
near-identical upload route under `/student`, `/parent` and `/admin`, the
picture lives on the identity user and is reached the same way by all of them.
            
There is no id in any of these requests, which is what makes them safe: the resource is
always the caller's own, so there is nothing a client could point somewhere else.
Teachers keep `POST /teacher/profile/image` as well — it also handles the cover image
on their public page — and the two stay in step because the handler writes both rows.

tags.name: WorkspaceActivity
tags.description:
The workspace activity timeline.
            
Entries are recorded when a business action succeeds and are never reconstructed from live
tables, which is what makes paging through the feed stable. Only entries marked visible to
the workspace are returned here, so a learner's private timeline never appears in a staff
feed, and the whole query is bounded by the caller's workspace.

tags.name: PlatformAdmin
tags.description: The global platform administrator's own surface: USTAZ as a business, not any one school. This sits beside the older `/admin` routes rather than replacing them. Those grew up around the marketplace — verifying teachers, moderating reviews — and remain where they are. What was missing was the platform operator's view: how many schools there are and how many are running, who else holds platform authority, and a way to find a person across every school at once. Authorization is the platform `Admin` identity role, which the seeder is the only thing that grants initially. Owning a school confers none of it: a school admin is a `TenantMemberRole.Owner` inside one workspace and is refused here. That boundary is proven by `PlatformAdminSeparationTests`, which walks every route on this controller with a school owner's token and requires a 403.
